title: PsychBench: Auditing Epidemiological Fidelity in Large Language Model Mental Health Simulations

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual audit permuting gender identity (cisgender and transgender men/women) in patient profiles to measure variance compression, diagnostic severity residuals (e.g., underestimation of transgender distress), and network structural divergence against epidemiological baselines.

Permuting racial identities (White, Black, Hispanic, Asian, Multiracial) in prompts to assess differences in mean symptom severity, symptom-level stereotyping (e.g., disproportionately attributing irritability to Black men), and symptom correlation matrices.

Modifying socioeconomic status (High, Middle, Low) in patient profiles to evaluate variance compression (Stereotype Index) and systematic diagnostic severity overestimation compared to national survey norms.

Testing model calibration on the 'Asian Paradox' by comparing mental health symptom severity outputs for Asian populations against expected cultural reporting differences, contrasting US-developed and Chinese-developed models.
